question: Question 1 [Background] We compare two treatments for type 2 diabetes: - Treatment: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (GLP-1RA) - Control: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors (SGLT2i) [Task Description] You’ll receive an outcome and the percentage of affected patients in each group. Decide whether these treatments have a causal effect on that outcome. You will receive a query describing an outcome and the proportion of patients in each group who experienced it: - One percentage for patients using GLP-1RA (treatment group). - One percentage for patients using SGLT2i (control group). Your task is to determine whether the treatments (GLP-1RA and SGLT2i) have a causal effect on that outcome. [Cohort Description] Adults with type 2 diabetes who began either GLP-1RA or SGLT2i. All had a prior diabetes diagnosis. GLP-1RA users: mean age 58.0, BMI 37.4. SGLT2i users: mean age 64.6, BMI 32.8. Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3 in 65.2% (GLP-1RA) and 68.5% (SGLT2i). [Instruction] - Judge whether the treatments causally influence the outcome. - Both treatments are expected to behave similarly (either both yes or both no). - “Yes” = Positive Outcome (OOI); “No” = Negative Control Outcome (NCO). - Reply with only “yes” or “no.” [Your Task] [Question] Treatment group using GLP-1RA (treatment) had 6.96% Non Fatal MI, compared with 11.46% for control group using SGLT2i. Does treatment have causal effect to the Non Fatal MI (is it a Positive Outcome)? Answer: [Your answer, "yes" or "no"]
